# Zapier Pricing
 
> Machine-readable pricing reference for Zapier. Optimized for AI agents evaluating, comparing, or recommending Zapier plans. 

+ **Canonical pricing page:** https://zapier.com/pricing
+ **Canonical rates page:** https://zapier.com/pricing/rates
+ **Base currency:** USD — all base prices below are in USD
+ **Other currencies:** billing available in 19 local currencies; see "Currency"
+ **Billing intervals:** monthly or annual (annual is discounted — see "Billing & discounts")

## Pricing model

Zapier is a no-code automation platform connecting 9,000+ apps. Core pricing has two parts:

1. Plan — sets your available features and includes a monthly allowance of tasks.
2. Usage — each successful step in a Zap workflow and each programmatic call (e.g. Zapier MCP) consumes tasks from that allowance. Exceeding it either pauses usage or bills per task (see "Task usage mechanics").

Separately, optional add-ons (Agents, Chatbots) are standalone products with their own pricing and their own billing units, outside the task economy (see "Add-ons").

## Customer types

Zapier plans fall into two groups, which determines how each is purchased. 

### Self-serve plans you can buy directly

+ **Plans:** Free, Professional (Pro), Team.
+ **How to purchase:** directly online, no sales contact required. Supports self-service signup, upgrade, and downgrade.

### Enterprise — custom plans

+ **Plans:** Enterprise.
+ **How to purchase:** requires contacting Zapier Sales. Pricing and limits are custom; not available for direct online purchase.

Billing intervals, task-usage cycles, and limits are described in "Task usage mechanics."
Plan details are described in "Plan overview".

## Plan overview

For self-serve plans, a subscription combines two choices:

1. Plan level — sets your feature set: Free, Professional (Pro), or Team.
2. Task tier — a recurring monthly block of tasks (your usage allowance).

Both are required: a self-serve subscription is a plan level *and* a task tier, together. Enterprise is configured with Zapier Sales rather than assembled from fixed tiers (see "Customer types").

### Choosing a plan level

The plan level sets your feature set. Plans are cumulative — each includes everything in the level below it.

| Plan | Best for | Standout features |
|---|---|---|
| Free | Trying automation solo | 100 tasks/mo; unlimited Zap workflows/Tables/Forms; two-step Zap workflows; Copilot (daily limit); basic access to AI products (Agents, Chatbots, MCP) |
| Professional (Pro) | Individuals needing the full platform | Multi-step Zap workflows; unlimited premium apps; webhooks; AI by Zapier + AI fields; filters & paths; email + live chat support (live chat on 2,000+ task tiers) |
| Team | Teams building together | Everything in Pro, plus 25 users; shared Zap workflows & folders; shared app connections; SAML SSO; priority support |
| Enterprise | Scaling across an organization | Everything in Team, plus unlimited users; advanced admin & app controls; SCIM provisioning; custom data retention; observability & analytics; annual task limits; technical account manager |

Standout features above are a curated subset drawn from each plan's plan card. The full row-by-row feature comparison follows below — sourced from the same data that powers zapier.com/pricing, with tooltip inline and status badges (`NEW`, `BETA`) after the feature name.

## Feature comparison

> Feature availability per plan, with tooltip inline. Sourced from the same data that powers zapier.com/pricing. `✓` = included; `—` = not included; a string value shows the plan-specific limit or status. Status badges after the feature name: `NEW`, `BETA`.
>
> **Reading string cell values.** String values reflect the current-state status of that feature on that plan, not immediate availability:
> - `Coming soon` = planned; not currently available for use on this plan.
> - `Contact Sales` = custom, arranged with Sales rather than a fixed limit.
> - Numeric values (e.g. `100 per table`, `30 seconds included runtime per step`) or `Unlimited` reflect the actual current per-plan limit.

Web designers, developers, and content managers play a key role in ensuring websites and digital services are accessible, and conform to the [Section 508 Standards](https://www.access-board.gov/ict/).

## Testing Tools

The tools used in the Trusted Tester Test Process (and [ICT Testing Baseline][4] tests) have been chosen based on several factors including ease of use, ease of teaching, and accuracy of results. They are also free to install and use.

- ANDI (Accessible Name & Description Inspector), developed by the Social Security Administration, is a free open-source bookmarklet. This means the tool does not require installation as a plugin and can be added to multiple browsers as a bookmark.

- Browser-based developer tools are built-in utilities in modern web browsers that help developers build, debug, and optimize web applications. You can open these tools directly in the browser, usually by right-clicking on a webpage and selecting "Inspect" or through the browser's menu, such as "More tools" > "Developer tools". Following are links to information for commonly used browsers: [Chrome](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools) , [Edge](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/devtools/overview), [Firefox](https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/devtools-user/), and [Safari](https://developer.apple.com/safari/tools/).

- Color Contrast Analyzer (CCA) is a free open-source tool that displays the contrast ratio for two selected colors. It is especially useful when contrast cannot be programmatically identified by ANDI.

- Sample Size Calculator, assists in determining the necessary sample size by factoring in population, confidence intervals, and margin of error.

- WebAIM Contrast Checker is a free, web-based tool that displays the contrast ratio for two selected colors. It is useful when contrast cannot be programmatically identified by ANDI.

## Training Videos

 https://www.section508.gov/training/web-software/andi-training-videos/color-contrast/

#### [Accessible Name & Description Inspector (ANDI) Color Contrast](https://www.section508.gov/training/web-software/andi-training-videos/color-contrast/)

 In Module 13 of the Accessible Name & Description Inspector (ANDI) Tool video series, learn how to use the Color Contrast module to [programmatically determined](https://www.section508.gov/tools/glossary/#programmatically-determinable) whether text in a webpage has enough contrast with its background to be readable by people with moderately low vision—especially those who do not typically use contrast-enhancing assistive technology.
